trusted_external_entities.entity_description: Validator who controls BLS key and wants to set withdrawal credentials via BLSToExecutionChange
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Validators are authenticated via BLS signature verification. Only the holder of the validator's BLS private key can create a valid BLSToExecutionChange message. However, the protocol cannot determine if the current key holder is the legitimate owner or an attacker who compromised the keys. Claims are cryptographically verified but ownership disputes require out-of-band resolution.
trusted_external_entities.authentication_mechanism: BLS cryptographic signature over withdrawal change parameters

trusted_external_entities.entity_description: Entity running a beacon node who voluntarily loads the broadcast file for message filtering
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Node operators voluntarily participate in the broadcast file filtering mechanism. They are trusted to correctly load and honor the broadcast file, but their participation is not enforced. The security mechanism relies on sufficient node operator adoption to be effective.

trusted_external_entities.entity_description: Entity submitting BLSToExecutionChange claims to community repository for verification
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Anyone can submit claims to the community repository. Claims must pass cryptographic signature verification before acceptance. Submitters are untrusted - the verification process validates claims, not submitters. Malicious submitters could attempt to submit fraudulent claims for validators they don't control.
trusted_external_entities.authentication_mechanism: None - claims validated by BLS signature verification, not submitter identity

trusted_external_entities.entity_description: Other beacon nodes in the P2P network that propagate BLSToExecutionChange messages
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: P2P peers are untrusted network participants. They may propagate both legitimate and malicious BLSToExecutionChange messages. The broadcast file filtering mechanism exists specifically because peers cannot be trusted - nodes must filter incoming messages against the pre-verified broadcast file to protect against conflicting messages from attackers.
trusted_external_entities.authentication_mechanism: None - messages validated by local filtering and signature verification

trusted_external_entities.entity_description: External user or contract deploying a new smart contract
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Any funded account can deploy contracts with arbitrary bytecode. The EIP-170 size limit exists specifically because deployers are untrusted - without limits, attackers could deploy arbitrarily large contracts causing DoS conditions for light clients during verification. The 24576 byte limit bounds verification work.
trusted_external_entities.authentication_mechanism: None - any funded account can deploy contracts

trusted_external_entities.entity_description: Ethereum P2P network propagating blocks containing contract creations
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: The P2P network is an untrusted data source. Blocks received from the network must be fully validated, including contract size checks. The EIP-170 size limit ensures that even malicious blocks can be validated in bounded time, preventing DoS attacks against light clients.
trusted_external_entities.authentication_mechanism: None - blocks validated cryptographically by receiving nodes

boundary_edges.data_flow_description: Validator prepares and submits signed BLSToExecutionChange message to set withdrawal credentials
Node operator configures beacon node with verified broadcast file for message filtering
Submitter uploads claim file to community repository for cryptographic verification
P2P peer sends BLSToExecutionChange message which must be filtered against broadcast file
Contract deployer submits contract creation transaction with init code
Network delivers block containing contract creations requiring size validation

coverage_analysis.notes: EIP-4736 BLSToExecutionChange (spec_971a6836d654.json) has significant trust boundaries around validator claim submission and P2P message filtering. The broadcast file mechanism provides protection against attackers who may have compromised validator keys. EIP-7516 BLOBBASEFEE (spec_992bc6c80c60.json) has no external entities - it reads blob base fee from block header, an internal EVM operation. Cancun stack operations (spec_9ae6fad82126bfdf5ccca0c6ce2d9eae3d495793.json) has no external entities - stack push/pop are internal EVM operations with overflow/underflow protections. EIP-170 contract size limit (spec_9ef609c80325.json) has DoS prevention trust boundary - untrusted deployers and network peers are constrained by 24576 byte limit. EIP-1716 Petersburg (spec_a41fbcd70ac3.json) has no external entities - consensus fork activation is internal protocol operation disabling EIP-1283 to mitigate reentrancy attack vectors.
